title: Answering a job sent back
eyebrow: Two board faults closed a circle around any job its reader turns down. You told me to fix them in a fresh copy first — this is that.

content.label: What is being fixed
content.lead: Two rules that are each sensible alone and together leave a job with no way forward.

rows: A piece of work counts as waiting whenever anything above it is waiting
a piece waiting only on the reading of its own job can be picked up — that reading is waiting for exactly that piece
A stage counts as built the moment any one piece of it is finished
a stage is built when every piece of it is finished

blocks.text: The first is what locks the objections away. The second is what tells the board a job has nothing left to build when it plainly does, which is how starting anything else got refused too.

Both watched happening rather than argued from the code, against the live board: four pieces of building work open, the board reporting that job's building as finished, all four reported as waiting, and the only thing they wait on is the reading that is waiting for those four.

content.label: In and landed
content.lead: Both fixed, and the four objections can now be picked up.

blocks.text: The board now says that job has building left to do, and its four objections are free to be started. The reading still holds the job shut, which is right — it goes back for a second reading once they are answered.
One more job was stuck in exactly the same way and is freed by the same change. The fault was never particular to mine, which is what made it worth fixing rather than escaping.

Held to it by the board's own checks: twenty-five, all green, six of them new. A piece under a shut job goes through, while the shut job itself, a hold that is not a reading, an ordinary card, a reading already passed and a board that did not answer each still refuse.

Checked by re-running the very script that showed the lock, unchanged: everything it printed as stuck now reads as free, and the reading still holds the job. Not a claim that it should work — the same measurement, before and after.
Both fixes were then cut out on purpose, one at a time, and the checks watched go red on each before being put back. A check that only ever passes proves nothing.

content.label: What is not being touched
content.lead: The reading itself keeps every tooth it has.

blocks.text: A job still cannot be finished around an objection, a reading lock is still never opened by the session it holds, and the job that is shut stays shut until a reader passes it. The only change is that its own answers can be started.

The copy of the work the shut job was using is gone, which is what let this one start. It held nothing that was not already banked, so nothing was lost, and that job gets a copy of its own when it is picked up again.

decisions.title: The waiting rule is narrowed, not removed
decisions.why: Work waiting on an ordinary card must still stay put — that is what stops two people building the same thing in the wrong order. Only the reading of a piece's own job is excused, because that reading is waiting on the piece.

decisions.title: Both faults are fixed in one go
decisions.why: They are the same misreading of what is left of a job, they sit in the same place, and fixing one without the other leaves the circle closed.

next.if_nothing: Nothing moves: the stopping-rule job stays shut and no new job can start.
